answer.why: As an insider I laughed at once. 'Confirmed and substantive' is exactly the phrase you see when someone's appointment stops being acting or on probation, and only people who have sat through the HR paperwork would pick it as a title. It signals the developer knows the service, which makes me trust the details will be right. 'Minister Salary' is the obvious headline hook and I'd probably tap it out of curiosity too, but it feels like a cheap jibe at a topic every Singaporean already has opinions on.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical or political-bait game about the benchmark formula and whether ministers are overpaid. I'd expect a punchy, slightly cynical tone, a climb-to-the-top race for the big number, and probably some details wrong about how people actually reach politics. It might be fun but shallow, and I'd brace to wince.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, insider-flavoured career sim about the actual texture of the service: appraisal wording, acting appointments, grades, postings, waiting to be confirmed. I'd expect humour that rewards people who have lived it, with a quieter, more accurate feel. The risk is that outsiders will have no idea what it means and scroll past, and the ampersand makes it look like a law firm.

best_moment.what: Giving full disclosure in the background check and having it pay off. It matched how vetting actually rewards candour, and it was the one time a principled choice felt properly repaid.

worst_moment.what: Adding the fourth pillar that looked bolted on. Nothing I did changed the result, and the whole year felt like a shrug.

answer.held_back_by: Visibility. I was honest and competent but never played the reputation game, so REP stayed at 50 while INTEG and COMP were maxed out. The game seems to say that being clean is not enough without being seen.
answer.ending_fair_why: Losing at 48.2% with maxed integrity and competence felt like the game saying nothing I did mattered. 'It was never going to be about you anyway' is probably true of GRC contests, but I got no sense of what I could have changed, so it landed as arbitrary rather than tragic.
answer.chase_next: Win the ward, or get the single seat. I would build REP early, even at some cost to integrity, to see whether the game lets me reach 60 and whether the political ending differs.
answer.play_again_why: I want to know whether REP can be built without selling out. I also want to see whether the people I helped ever come back, because that never paid off in this run.
